title: Cone model of a prescribed top cell over constant field coefficients
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and assume evaluation at $T$ sends epimorphisms of sheaves of sets to surjections. Let $k$ be a field and $k_T$ its constant sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Work in the unbounded derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(k_T))$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $a\leq b$ be integers, let $N$ have $H^q(N)=0$ outside $[a,b]$, and fix finite integers $r_q\geq0$ and isomorphisms $\theta_q:k_T^{\oplus r_q}\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(N)$ for $a\leq q\leq b$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Define zero-differential cochain complexes
$$A=k_T^{\oplus r_b}[-b],\qquad V=\bigoplus_{q=a}^b k_T^{\oplus r_q}[-q],\qquad W=\bigoplus_{q=a}^{b-1}k_T^{\oplus r_q}[-q],$$
and let $i:A\to V$ be the top summand inclusion. Write $Q$ for localization of complexes into the derived category. Let $u:Q(A)\to N$ induce $\theta_b$, and let $Q(A)\xrightarrow{u}N\to C\to Q(A)[1]$ be any distinguished triangle. There exists an isomorphism $\varphi:Q(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}N$ inducing the prescribed $\theta_q$. For every such isomorphism, $u=\varphi\circ Q(i)$, and there is an isomorphism of distinguished triangles from the given triangle to the cone triangle of $Q(i)$ whose first two components are $\mathrm{id}_{Q(A)}$ and $\varphi^{-1}$. The literal mapping cone satisfies a chain isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Cone}(i)\cong W\oplus D,$$
where $D^{b-1}=D^b=k_T^{\oplus r_b}$, $d_D^{b-1}=\mathrm{id}$, and all other terms and differentials of $D$ are zero. The degree-minus-one family $h$ with $h^b=\mathrm{id}$ and all other components zero satisfies $d_Dh+hd_D=\mathrm{id}_D$. In particular there are derived isomorphisms $C\cong Q(\operatorname{Cone}(i))\cong Q(W)$. For every site object $U\to T$, with $(-)|_U$ the termwise restriction to the localized site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], $W|_U$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], and for every degree-zero $k_U$-module sheaf $F$ there is a derived isomorphism
$$ (C|_U)\otimes^L_{k_U} F\cong\bigoplus_{q=a}^{b-1}F^{\oplus r_q}[-q] $$
[def-weil-derived-tensor]. Thus, when $a<b$, $C$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b-1]$ after every restriction [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], and $H^q(C)$ is the constant free sheaf of rank $r_q$ for $a\leq q<b$, zero otherwise. When $a=b$, $W$ and $C$ are zero. Zero ranks and the empty scheme are allowed. No integral coefficient ring, quotient tower, or completeness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-projective-cohomology-split-model] with $U=T$ and $C=k_T$. Its evaluation hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis here, and its cohomology interval, finite ranks and specified isomorphisms are our $[a,b],r_q,\theta_q$. For a representative $Z$ of $N$ it gives a quasi-isomorphism $V\to Z$ inducing every $\theta_q$. Localizing and composing with the representing isomorphism gives $\varphi:Q(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}N$ with the required cohomology maps.

source.place: Tag 09C3, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex, final induction paragraph; prescribed splitting expanded by the cited projective-cohomology lemma.

proof.text: Now let $\varphi$ be ANY isomorphism inducing the prescribed $\theta_q$. The two maps $u$ and $\varphi Q(i)$ from $k_T^{\oplus r_b}[-b]$ induce the same $\theta_b$. In the natural generator bijection of [lem-sf-projective-cohomology-split-model], their images are therefore the same $r_b$ global sections of $H^b(N)$. Injectivity gives $u=\varphi Q(i)$. This proves the universal quantifier over $\varphi$, rather than just the equality for the splitting chosen in step 1.

source.place: Tag 064B, lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex; generator bijection as stated in the cited splitting lemma.

proof.text: The cone triangle of $i$ is distinguished after $Q$ by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The equality in step 2 is precisely the first commutative square with vertical maps $\mathrm{id}_{Q(A)}$ and $\varphi^{-1}$. Axiom TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] completes these two maps to a morphism from the given distinguished triangle to that cone triangle. Both first components are isomorphisms, so [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes the third component an isomorphism as well. Componentwise inverses give an isomorphism of triangles; in particular $C\cong Q(\operatorname{Cone}(i))$. No uniqueness of the third map is asserted.

proof.text: Use the literal mapping-cone matrix and the complementary lower/top inclusions and projections. Their four splitting identities give an explicit chain isomorphism Cone(i) ≅ W ⊕ Cone(id_A). The standard identity-cone homotopy contracts the second summand. Its components are zero unless the source is degree b; the displayed normalization follows from the cone inclusion/projection identities. The cone has free terms in b-1 and b and the differential is the identity under those identifications. Localization identifies homotopic maps, so Q(Cone(id_A)) is zero. Additivity of Q and biproduct cancellation give Q(Cone(i)) ≅ Q(W).

source.place: definition-cone, explicit matrix differential; Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category.

proof.text: For every site object U, use exact slice restriction [lem-sf-site-perfect-restriction-exact] and the derived-restriction comparison [lem-sf-site-perfect-derived-restriction-iso] to transport C ≅ Q(W) to C|U ≅ Q(W|U). Restriction is additive [lem-sf-site-perfect-restriction-additive] and preserves finite coproducts. Restrict the coproduct of units defining each finite free term and reindex ULift(Fin r_q) along Equiv.ulift. This identifies its restriction with the finite coproduct of slice units. Zero terms and zero differentials remain zero. No comparison with the pro-etale site of the scheme U is required.

source.place: Section 03DH, definition-localize-ringed-site; sites.tex Tag 00XR, lemma-when-shriek, and Section 00XZ; proetale.tex Definition 09AE and the localized-site identification.

proof.text: Each restricted term of W is a finite sum of tensor units, hence flat: the unit is flat, finite biproducts preserve flatness, and the site/monoidal tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits] transfers categorical flatness to site flatness. Since W is bounded above, [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] makes W|U K-flat. Apply [lem-sf-ringed-kflat-single-tensor-comparison] to compute its tensor with a degree-zero module F by the additive termwise tensor functor. The tensor functor preserves finite coproducts and takes unit ⊗ F to F. A zero-differential complex supported on [a,b-1] is canonically the coproduct of its single-degree terms; construct this isomorphism by the degreewise coproduct universal property. This yields the asserted tensor model. Its support proves the Tor bound. The canonical cycles/homology maps of the zero-differential W identify its homology with its terms, giving the stated cohomology of C. If a=b every term of W is zero, so W and C vanish. Finite empty coproducts, zero ranks, negative degrees, and the empty scheme are covered by the same constructions.
